questions.question: Describe buses and trains as public transport in South African cities, with advantages and disadvantages.
questions.expected_answer: Municipal buses such as Metrobus and Golden Arrow, commuter buses such as Putco, often subsidised, and bus rapid transit systems such as Rea Vaya, A Re Yeng and MyCiTi with dedicated lanes, carry many people cheaply and reduce cars, but follow fixed routes and timetables and can be slow in traffic. Metrorail commuter trains run by PRASA and the Gautrain carry very large numbers cheaply and avoid road traffic, but only run where there are tracks, stations may be far away, and many services have been unreliable because of cable theft, vandalism and broken trains.

questions.question: Describe the minibus taxi industry and its advantages and disadvantages.
questions.expected_answer: Minibus taxis are the most used public transport in South Africa, privately owned minibuses run through taxi associations, that grew rapidly in the 1980s. Advantages: many routes including townships, informal settlements and rural areas, frequent early services, stopping almost anywhere, links with stations and ranks, and many jobs. Disadvantages: fares can be higher than subsidised buses and trains, some vehicles are old or overloaded, unsafe driving and accidents, and route conflicts that have sometimes turned violent; the Taxi Recapitalisation Programme helped replace old vehicles.

questions.question: Compare private transport options and explain why many commutes are long.
questions.expected_answer: Cars offer comfort and door-to-door freedom but are expensive, cause congestion because most carry one or two people, need parking and pollute. Bicycles are cheap, clean and healthy but can be dangerous without cycle lanes and suit short distances. Many people walk because they cannot afford fares. Choice depends on income, distance, cost, time, safety and availability. Apartheid laws such as the Group Areas Act of 1950 placed black South Africans far from city jobs, and this pattern remains, so many workers travel for hours and spend a large share of income on transport, for example R25 each way for 22 days is R1 100 a month.
